Level 1 · Introduction · Week 7

Hello, Python!

Text code is just blocks written as words — and Python is picky.

What you will learn

  • How to open, run and save a program in Thonny.
  • How to make Python say things with print, and leave notes with comments.
  • How to make the turtle draw a square with forward and left.
  • How to read a red error message like a detective.

Warm-up: Spot the difference

Python is very picky. On each card, one line works and one line confuses Python. Circle the difference. Check the line that works.

Card Line A Line B
1 ☐ print("Hello") ☐ Print("Hello")
2 ☐ t.forwad(100) ☐ t.forward(100)
3 ☐ t.left(90 ☐ t.left(90)
4 ☐ t.left(90) ☐ t.Left(90)
5 ☐ print(Hi there) ☐ print("Hi there")

The big idea: blocks become words

In Scratch you snapped blocks together. In Python you type the same ideas as words. The computer still does the lines in order, from top to bottom.

Scratch block Python line
→ the green Run button (or F5)
→ t.forward(100)
→ t.left(90)
→ print("Hello!")

Meet Thonny

Thonny is the app where we write Python. It has three important parts.

TipWhere did my turtle go?

The turtle window sometimes hides behind Thonny. Click the Python icon in the Dock at the bottom of the screen.

Every turtle program has the same shape

import turtle            # 1. get the turtle toolbox
t = turtle.Turtle()      # 2. make a turtle and call it t
t.forward(100)           # 3. your drawing commands go here
t.left(90)
turtle.done()            # 4. keep the window open at the end

Lines that start with # are comments. Python skips them. They are notes for people.

Exercise7.1: Hello, Python!

Folder: week07/ex-hello-python. Open starter.py and press Run.

  1. Add three print lines: who is coding today (a nickname), your favorite game or animal, and a goodbye that uses the word bye.

  2. Press Run after every new line.

Done looks like: four different lines in the Shell.

Exercise7.2: My First Square

Folder: week07/ex-first-square. The turtle draws one side already. Add the other three sides: each side is t.forward(100) then t.left(90). Done looks like: a closed square — the turtle ends where it started.

Reading a red error message

When Python is confused, it stops and shows red text in the Shell. Don’t panic — it is a clue!

Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "starter.py", line 12, in <module>
    Print("Typo hunt: fixed!")
NameError: name 'Print' is not defined

  • line 12 tells you where to look.

  • The last line tells you what confused Python: it does not know the word Print.

Exercise7.3: Typo Hunt

Folder: week07/ex-typo-hunt. This program should draw a flag on a pole, but it has 4 typos. Run it, read the red message, fix one typo, run again. Write down what you fixed:

Line The typo was I changed it to

TipSave your work safely

Exercises: press Cmd+S to save starter.py in its folder. New programs go in Documents/my-python. Use names that say what the program does, like flag-drawing.py. Never call a file turtle.py: Python would get mixed up with the real turtle!

Reflect

What was different about typing code instead of dragging blocks?

Which typo was the hardest to spot? What will you check first next time?

New words

Python
A text programming language. We type words instead of snapping blocks.
Thonny
The app where we write and run Python programs.
Editor
The top part of Thonny where you write your program.
Shell
The bottom part of Thonny where Python shows messages and errors.
print
A command that shows words in the Shell: print("Hi") .
Comment
A note for people that starts with # . Python skips it.
Syntax error
A typo or missing bracket that stops Python from understanding your code.
Bug
A mistake in a program. Every programmer makes them!

Homework: Triangle Time

15–20 minutes. Do Core first; Challenge and Creative are optional.

CoreTriangle Time (about 10 minutes)

In Thonny, open week07/hw-triangle/starter.py. The turtle already draws one side.

  1. Add the code for the other two sides. Each side is t.forward(120) then t.left(120).

  2. Why 120? The turtle must turn all the way round (360 degrees) in 3 corners: 3 × 120 = 360.

No computer at home? Write the whole program here and type it in next week:

ChallengeBe the turtle

Don’t run it yet! Read this program and draw what the turtle will draw in the box. The turtle starts at the dot, facing right. Then type it in and check.

t.forward(100)
t.left(90)
t.forward(50)
t.left(90)
t.forward(100)

What letter or shape does it look like? (blank to fill in)

CreativeMy initial

Plan the first letter of your nickname with straight lines only (E, F, H, L, T, Z work well). Draw it on the grid. Write the steps next to it, like F 100, L 90, F 50. Then try it in Thonny in a new file saved as my-python/initial.py.
